name: ONiO.zero
description: Wireless MCU integrating a radio and energy-harvesting power management.

pins.notes: The official feature overview does not supply a revision-specific package pinout. The user identifies VMAIN as a bidirectional storage connection for a capacitor, supercapacitor or battery, with a 250 mV minimum operating voltage. Maximum voltage, charge/discharge behavior and package pin numbers remain uncharacterized. See characterization.json vmain_storage. VMAIN is not yet implemented by the runnable load model.

radio.notes: Official feature overview advertises Bluetooth LE 5.4 (1M, 2M, 125/500 kbit/s coded PHY), IEEE 802.15.4-2020 using 2.4 GHz O-QPSK, and programmable TX power from -40 to 0 dBm. The 250 kbit/s entry maps the declared 2.4 GHz O-QPSK PHY to its standard data rate. These are product-level capabilities, not revision-specific stack certification or characterized current/timing data. Do not substitute older ONiO.zero transmitter-only descriptions for this feature set. User-provided powers and timings are recorded separately in characterization.json and the runnable approximation; timing_status here describes manufacturer-source characterization.

simulation.scope: User-provided fixed-power CPU, sleep, BLE 1M and IEEE 802.15.4 states, with explicit wake/startup/turnaround/sleep-entry timing in characterization.json. These values are not manufacturer-verified catalog operating points. Logical power input only. Harvesting, storage, output rails and automatic radio traffic remain outside this load approximation.
blockers: Obtain revision-specific datasheet, package pinout and measurement conditions.
Characterize voltage dependence, other PHYs/TX powers and combined CPU/radio states.
Model harvesting, storage, cold start, conversion losses and brownout before predicting energy-limited operation.

Characterize VMAIN maximum voltage, charging behavior, conversion losses and cutoff/restart thresholds; implement a bidirectional storage path for capacitor, supercapacitor or compatible battery attachments. The user has confirmed the minimum operating voltage as 250 mV.
